## Preparing for the exam

### TRUST Recreational Drone Certification
Start with obtaining your TRUST Recreational Drone Certification. [Link](https://trust.pilotinstitute.com/?gc_id=13607090805&h_ga_id=127809592470&h_ad_id=529093306996&h_keyword_id=kwd-365197151701&h_keyword=%2Btrust%20%2Bdrone&h_placement=&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=13607090805&gbraid=0AAAAACtJPalZDGIH0H5SX6nHsPWMRLQWL&gclid=CjwKCAiAkbbMBhB2EiwANbxtbSJ-P5hQU2vxRQqHQR672Y8qiKLVxT1nLWYp57unT84MqXrT3fgOLhoCLuQQAvD_BwE).

It is not required to obtain your Part 107, but is useful as a first overview of drone regulation. 
You'll create an account and go though ~20 minutes of training explaining what you can and can't do as a recreational flyer. 
There are four quizzes you take as you review the material, and at the end you receive a pdf of your certificate (They delete your account after you download the certificate, so make sure you save it somewhere safe.) 


### Eligibility

Information about the exam itself can be found [here](https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators/become_a_drone_pilot).
It also walks though the whole process. 
That is the definitive source, and trumps any information found here. 

The general requirements are as follows:

- Be at least 16 years old
- Be able to read, speak, write, and understand English
- Be in a physical and mental condition to safely fly a drone
- Pass the initial aeronautical knowledge exam: "Unmanned Aircraft General – Small (UAG)"

### Studying
There is a lot out there for test prep. This section is a mix of what I did and the resources from the CE Drone Measurments Class being piloted at BYU. 

- Study for the test intensly several days before you take the test. 
    There is so much that you need to know only for the test that cramming is what I recommend. 
    Plan a day for the test, set aside several hours each day before hand for studying, and then schedule the test. 
- I watched [this guy's](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u3AwQZTbtfc) video when I first started studying and right before I took the test.
    It's a good overview of the topics on the test, but is nowhere near comprehensive. 
- I watched the 12 study guide videos made by [this guy](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLRd2JSjVHovGabIuGeoupZgkzGmdys4Ol). 
    He's pretty long winded and interesting, but he covered most things on the test. 
    His videos are long, so watch at atleast 1.5x speed. 

Other Resources:
- [This](https://free-faa-exam.kingschools.com/drone-pilot) is an test exam that might be useful.
    I didn't use it, so I can't say if it is good or not. 

Important things to note about the exam:

- It costs a couple hundred dollars, like other licecing exams. 
- You are given 2 hours to take the test. If you've prepared, you shouldn't have much problem completting the test. 
- There are 60 questions on the test, with the typical format being 3 options per question. 
- You must get 70% of the questions right to pass. This is 42 questions. 
- Your licence will be valid for 2 years from licening date. If you maintain it, you won't have to take the test again. 
- The closest testing center is at the Provo airport through UVU, but there are other ones around

## Registering for the Part 107

### Creating a FAA Account

This will give you a FAA tracking number, which will be needed to register for your exam and licence. 

1. Go to the [iacra website](https://iacra.faa.gov/IACRA/SelectRoles.aspx).
2. Select Applicant, scrolldown and click "agree to TOS and continue".
3. Fillout the User Profile Information. Skip the section that says Airman certificate number.
    Enter personal info, security questions, and create a username and password. 
4. You will have to set up a authenticator app, either here or when registoring for the exam. 

### Registering for the Exam

1. Go to [psiexams](https://faa.psiexams.com/faa/login).
2. Sign in using the same login for your FAA account.
3. Search for and select "Unmanned Aircraft General - Small (UAG)". Confirm that you selected the correct test.
4. Follow the prompts to fillout the information for signing up for the test. 
    (I can't reregister for the test to fully outline the process, but it is straight forward)
